# Description of the package

This package is useful for counting missing values for various groups. 
Here are some features that this package can conduct.

1. Ungrouped missing values for different columns

2. Displaying missing values, grouped by a specified variable in the output table.

# Installation instructions

This package is available for free public download (with citation) from GitHub. Install the "devtools" package if you do not already have it on your R studio.
Use the following code to directly install the package by pasting this message directly into the R console. If successfully installed you are likely to get a message like this at the end of the loading code in your R console "DONE (assignmentB2JeremyDykstra)". 

```{r, message = FALSE}
#install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github("UBC-STAT545-F2026/assignmentB2JeremyDykstra") 
```

# How to use this package, with examples

After installing the package from GitHub, load the package into your R studio using the below code. 

```{r, message = FALSE}
library(assignmentB2JeremyDykstra)
```

The primary function in the package is named "count_all_missing_by_group". You can call the function by selecting the following parameters. 

Parameters in the function
1. data (name of data)
2. group_col (Variable name)
3. .groups = "drop" (ungrouped output) or .groups = "keep" (grouped table)

When you put it all together it looks like this: function(data, group_col, .groups = "drop"). 

See below for two examples using an air quality dataset by Month in either the ungrouped or grouped table.  

```{r}
count_all_missing_by_group(airquality, Month) #ungrouped table
count_all_missing_by_group(airquality, Month, .groups = "keep") #grouped table
```
